lunch.name: Caldo Verde (Portuguese Green Soup)
lunch.description: Traditional Portuguese lunch - simple potato and collard green soup with chorizo. Peasant soup that became national favorite
instructions: Heat olive oil, sauté diced onion and minced garlic until soft
Add diced potatoes and broth, bring to boil
Reduce heat and simmer 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender
Slice chorizo and add to soup, cook 5 minutes
Finely slice collard greens and add to soup just before serving
Season with salt and pepper
Serve hot with crusty bread on the side
lunch.notes: Add greens at last moment to preserve color and texture. Can be made vegetarian without chorizo
lunch.fun_fact: Caldo Verde is traditional Portuguese lunch, simple peasant soup that became national favorite. Often served at celebrations
alternatives: Use spinach instead of collard greens
Add smoked ham instead of chorizo

dinner.name: Francesinha (French Sandwich)
dinner.description: Portuguese grilled sandwich with meat, ham, and cheese covered in beer sauce - iconic Porto sandwich
ingredients: 4 slices of Portuguese white bread or similar
80g sliced cheese (typically cheddar or similar melting cheese)
2 slices of gruyere or similar hard cheese
instructions: Make the sauce: melt butter in pan, add flour to create roux
Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant
Stir in tomato paste, cook 2 minutes
Add beef broth, beer, and bay leaves
Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens
Season with salt and pepper, remove bay leaves
Meanwhile, prepare sandwiches: layer bread with roast beef, ham, and sliced cheese
Press down to compact, then top with second slice of bread
Place gruyere slices on top of sandwiches
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat
Fry sandwiches until bread is golden and cheese begins to melt (3-4 minutes per side)
Transfer to serving plates
Pour hot beer sauce generously over sandwiches
Optional: fry eggs and place on top of sandwich
Serve immediately while hot with sauce
dinner.notes: The sauce must be hot when poured over sandwich. Traditional recipe includes fried egg on top
dinner.fun_fact: Francesinha originated in Porto and the name means 'Little French Girl', though it's entirely Portuguese
